roblox-headless-renderer

See Roblox files without opening Studio.
Pictures and plain facts about your UI and 3D builds, in seconds, from the command line.

--- Point `rhr` at a Roblox file (`.rbxm`, `.rbxmx`, `.rbxl`, `.rbxlx`), a Rojo project, a UI story or a Creator Store link, and it tells you what's there: **a PNG to look at, and JSON that says where everything is, what's clickable, and what looks broken.** It was built for **AI agents** that make Roblox games and need to check their own work, and it's just as handy when **you** want a quick look at a file, a free model or a pull request without starting Studio. It runs on Windows, macOS and Linux, including CI and cloud sandboxes: no display, GPU or running Studio needed. ## Quick start ```sh uv tool install roblox-headless-renderer # or: pip install --pre roblox-headless-renderer ``` Then, on any file of yours: ```sh rhr ui MyGame.rbxl --out ui.png # the screen UI, as a PNG rhr scene MyGame.rbxl --out world.png # the 3D world, as a PNG rhr check MyGame.rbxl # UI mistakes a player would notice ``` That's it: no setup step. The first run fetches anything missing (see [what gets downloaded](#details)). Just want to try it once? `uvx roblox-headless-renderer ui MyGui.rbxmx --out gui.png` runs it without installing anyth

-- Ask Roblox where to download assets, as the user signed in to Roblox Studio here.
--
--   lune run fetch-locations.luau < ids.json
--
-- stdin is a JSON array of asset ids (strings). Studio's saved login is read here
-- (Lune's roblox.getAuthCookie) and sent only to Roblox's asset delivery batch
-- endpoint, the same service Studio asks. It is never printed, written or handed back
-- to RHR. What is printed is one JSON object, id -> {location, type} or {code, message}:
-- a location is a short-lived signed link on Roblox's CDN for that one file, not the
-- login. Prints "nologin" when there is no saved login.
local net = require("@lune/net")
local process = require("@lune/process")
local roblox = require("@lune/roblox")
local serde = require("@lune/serde")
local stdio = require("@lune/stdio")
local task = require("@lune/task")

local BATCH = 256 -- the endpoint refuses more assets per request

local ok, cookie = pcall(roblox.getAuthCookie)
if not ok or not cookie or #cookie == 0 then
	print("nologin")
	process.exit(3)
end

local ids = serde.decode("json", stdio.readToEnd())
local results = {}
local pending = 0

local function ask(chunk)
	local body = {}
	for _, id in chunk do
		table.insert(body, { assetId = tonumber(id), requestId = id })
	end
	local okRequest, response = pcall(net.request, {
		url = "https://assetdelivery.roblox.com/v2/assets/batch",
		method = "POST",
		headers = {
			Cookie = cookie,
			["User-Agent"] = "roblox-headless-renderer",
			["Content-Type"] = "application/json",
		},
		body = serde.encode("json", body),
	})
	if not okRequest then
		for _, id in chunk do
			results[id] = { code = 0, message = "request failed" }
		end
	elseif not response.ok then
		for _, id in chunk do
			results[id] = { code = response.statusCode, message = "batch refused" }
		end
	else
		for _, item in serde.decode("json", response.body) do
			local locations = item.locations
			if locations and locations[1] and locations[1].location then
				results[item.requestId] = { location = locations[1].location, type = item.assetTypeId }
			else
				local err = item.errors and item.errors[1] or {}
				results[item.requestId] = { code = err.code or 0, message = err.message or "no location" }
			end
		end
	end
	pending -= 1
end

for start = 1, #ids, BATCH do
	pending += 1
	task.spawn(ask, table.move(ids, start, math.min(start + BATCH - 1, #ids), 1, {}))
end
while pending > 0 do
	task.wait()
end
print(serde.encode("json", results))

-- rhr-ir.luau for many files in one Lune process (rhr.lune_worker).
--
-- Starting Lune and the script costs about half a second, most of what converting a
-- small XML model takes. The resident server keeps this loop running instead: it
-- compiles rhr-ir.luau once and runs it as a fresh chunk for every request, so no
-- state is shared between files.
--
-- Usage: lune run rhr-ir-serve.luau <path to rhr-ir.luau>
-- Each request is one line on stdin: source TAB out TAB profile. The reply on stdout is
-- what the script printed, one line each, then a line of ASCII 30 followed by "ok" or
-- "error <message>". An empty line or the end of stdin ends the loop.

local fs = require("@lune/fs")
local luau = require("@lune/luau")
local process = require("@lune/process")
local stdio = require("@lune/stdio")

local bytecode = luau.compile(fs.readFile(process.args[1]))

while true do
  local line = stdio.readLine()
  if line == nil then break end
  line = string.gsub(line, "[\r\n]+$", "")
  if line == "" then break end
  local fields = string.split(line, "\t")
  local printed = {}
  local chunk = luau.load(bytecode, {
    debugName = "rhr-ir",
    environment = {
      print = function(...)
        local parts = table.pack(...)
        for index = 1, parts.n do parts[index] = tostring(parts[index]) end
        table.insert(printed, table.concat(parts, "\t", 1, parts.n))
      end,
    },
  })
  local ok, err = pcall(chunk, fields[1], fields[2], fields[3])
  local status = ok and "ok" or ("error " .. string.gsub(tostring(err), "[\r\n]+", " "))
  local body = table.concat(printed, "\n")
  stdio.write((#printed > 0 and (body .. "\n") or "") .. "\30" .. status .. "\n")
end

local roblox = require("@lune/roblox")
local fs = require("@lune/fs")
local serde = require("@lune/serde")
local process = require("@lune/process")

-- IR emitter. Dumps a Roblox model/place to JSON with real datatypes, so the

-- Effects that a script plays keep how to play them in attributes (the community's
-- EmitCount / EmitDelay / EmitDuration convention); the scene reads them to show the

-- JSON has no infinity; UISizeConstraint.MaxSize defaults to (inf, inf). Clamp to
-- a large finite sentinel the adapter reads as "unbounded".
local function finite(n)
  if n ~= n or n == math.huge or n == -math.huge then return 1e6 end
  return n
end

local B64 = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/"
local function base64(data: string): string
  local len = #data
  local out = buffer.create(math.ceil(len / 3) * 4)
  local o = 0
  for i = 1, len, 3 do
    local a, b, c = string.byte(data, i, i + 2)
    local n = a * 65536 + (b or 0) * 256 + (c or 0)
    buffer.writeu8(out, o, string.byte(B64, bit32.rshift(n, 18) + 1))
    buffer.writeu8(out, o + 1, string.byte(B64, bit32.band(bit32.rshift(n, 12), 63) + 1))
    buffer.writeu8(out, o + 2, if b then string.byte(B64, bit32.band(bit32.rshift(n, 6), 63) + 1) else 61)
    buffer.writeu8(out, o + 3, if c then string.byte(B64, bit32.band(n, 63) + 1) else 61)
    o += 4
  end
  return buffer.tostring(out)
end

local function conv(v, depth)
  depth = depth or 0
  if v == nil or depth > 5 then return nil end
  local t = typeof(v)
  if t == "Vector2" then return { X = finite(v.X), Y = finite(v.Y), _t = t } end
  if t == "Vector3" then return { X = finite(v.X), Y = finite(v.Y), Z = finite(v.Z), _t = t } end
  if t == "CFrame" then
    local x, y, z, r00, r01, r02, r10, r11, r12, r20, r21, r22 = v:GetComponents()
    return {
      X = x, Y = y, Z = z,
      R00 = r00, R01 = r01, R02 = r02,
      R10 = r10, R11 = r11, R12 = r12,
      R20 = r20, R21 = r21, R22 = r22,
      _t = t,
    }
  end
  if t == "UDim" then return { Scale = v.Scale, Offset = v.Offset, _t = t } end
  if t == "UDim2" then return { XS = v.X.Scale, XO = v.X.Offset, YS = v.Y.Scale, YO = v.Y.Offset, _t = t } end
  if t == "Color3" then return { R = v.R, G = v.G, B = v.B, _t = t } end
  if t == "Rect" then return { Min = conv(v.Min, depth + 1), Max = conv(v.Max, depth + 1), _t = t } end
  if t == "NumberRange" then return { Min = v.Min, Max = v.Max, _t = t } end
  if t == "EnumItem" then return { enum = tostring(v.EnumType), name = v.Name, value = v.Value, _t = t } end
  if t == "Font" then return { family = tostring(v.Family), weight = tostring(v.Weight), style = tostring(v.Style), _t = t } end
  if t == "ColorSequence" or t == "NumberSequence" then
    local kp = {}
    for _, k in ipairs(v.Keypoints) do
      local okE, env = pcall(function() return k.Envelope end)
      table.insert(kp, { Time = k.Time, Value = conv(k.Value, depth + 1), Envelope = okE and env or nil })
    end
    return { kind = t, keypoints = kp, _t = t }
  end
  if type(v) == "number" or type(v) == "string" or type(v) == "boolean" then return v end
  if t == "Content" then
    -- The bridge's Content object carries the asset URI in .Uri; tostring() gives
    -- the debug form "Content(Uri=rbxassetid://123)". An empty Content has no URI,
    -- and must drop the property rather than render the string "Content(None)".
    local u = v.Uri
    if u == nil then return nil end
    local s = tostring(u)
    if s == "" then return nil end
    return s
  end
  -- Unknown datatype: hand back nil so the caller can name it. Returning
  -- tostring(t) here ("CFrame") would look like a value and hide the gap.
  return nil
end

-- Property reads are the emitter's cost. One read per name per instance, and every
-- name the class does not have raises an error whose stack traceback the bridge
-- formats before we throw it away. On AnimationEditorGUI (1479 instances, 137 names)
-- that is 202,623 reads: 1970-2091ms for the read pass plus 2108ms for the
-- `<name>Content` retry that followed every miss, out of a 5.6s emit. 78% of those reads
-- are for names the class cannot have at all (Frame has 23 of the 137 allowlisted names,
-- TextLabel 39, UICorner 6). Lune bundles rbx-dom's reflection database, so the real
-- property set of a class is available without guessing: read the ones that exist,
-- skip the rest. A name the class *does* have is never skipped: skipping it would
-- be a silent drop, which is the one thing this emitter exists to prevent, so the
-- first instance of every class is still read in full and the outcome compared
-- with the database (report_class_filter_mismatches below, printed every run).
local reflect = roblox.getReflectionDatabase()
local class_props = {}
-- Classes the database does not have. They are read in full, so nothing is filtered
-- away, but they cannot be compared against a property list the database does not
-- hold: that comparison would report every name the class lacks as a mismatch.
local unknown_classes = {}

local function class_property_set(className)
  local cached = class_props[className]
  if cached then return cached end
  local set, cur, reached_root = {}, reflect:GetClass(className), false
  local guard = 0
  while cur and guard < 16 do
    for name in pairs(cur.Properties) do set[name] = true end
    if cur.Name == "Instance" or cur.Name == "Object" then reached_root = true end
    local ok, next_class = pcall(function() return reflect:GetClass(cur.Superclass) end)
    if not ok then break end
    cur = next_class
    guard = guard + 1
  end
  -- A class whose chain does not reach the root is a class we do not understand.
  -- Read everything for it rather than a subset.
  if not reached_root then
    -- A copy, not PROPS_SET itself: this table is handed out as a per-class answer and
    -- cached, so an alias would let any caller that extends it change the allowlist for
    -- every class and every later run in the same process.
    local full = {}
    for name in pairs(PROPS_SET) do full[name] = true end
    set = full
    unknown_classes[className] = true
  end
  class_props[className] = set
  return set
end

-- A property the database does not list but the bridge hands over would be lost by
-- the filter above, so the first instance of each class is read in full anyway and
-- the two answers are compared. The counters print on every run.
--
-- What this check does NOT cover, because it is only as wide as the database it compares
-- against: instance-level divergence. Property existence is a class-level fact in rbx-dom
-- and reading every instance in full is the cost this change exists to remove, so a
-- property only some instances of a class answer is invisible here. A read that comes back
-- nil, or as an instance reference, is not counted either: nil is how the bridge answers
-- for a property that exists without a value.
local verified_classes = {}
local filter_mismatches = { narrow = 0, wide = 0, names = {} }

local function verify_class(inst, set)
  if verified_classes[inst.ClassName] then return end
  verified_classes[inst.ClassName] = true
  if unknown_classes[inst.ClassName] then return end
  for _, name in ipairs(PROPS) do
    local ok, value = pcall(function() return inst[name] end)
    if ok and value ~= nil and typeof(value) ~= "Instance" then
      if not set[name] then
        filter_mismatches.narrow = filter_mismatches.narrow + 1
        if #filter_mismatches.names < 8 then
          table.insert(filter_mismatches.names, inst.ClassName .. "." .. name)
        end
      end
    elseif not ok and set[name] then
      if string.find(tostring(value), "is not a valid member of", 1, true) then
        filter_mismatches.wide = filter_mismatches.wide + 1
        if #filter_mismatches.names < 8 then
          table.insert(filter_mismatches.names, "!" .. inst.ClassName .. "." .. name)
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

-- Some property types have no default value registered in the Lua bridge, so
-- reading them raises "Failed to get property 'Image' - missing default value"
-- (current rbx-dom Content/ContentId accessors). The old code pcall'd each read
-- and dropped failures, which silently deleted every asset id in the model and
-- produced an IR that rendered without images. Recover those names from the XML
-- view of the same instance: the value is plain text there.
-- rbx-dom escapes "&", "<" and ">" in property text, so a recovered value is the XML
-- spelling of the string until this runs: `cheap & cheerful` reached the IR as itself.
local function unescape(text)
  if not string.find(text, "&", 1, true) then return text end
  text = string.gsub(text, "<", "<")
  text = string.gsub(text, ">", ">")
  text = string.gsub(text, """, '"')
  text = string.gsub(text, "&#(%d+);", function(code) return string.char(tonumber(code)) end)
  text = string.gsub(text, "'", "'")
  -- last, so an escaped entity in the file stays escaped text rather than turning into
  -- the character it names
  return (string.gsub(text, "&", "&"))
end

-- A recovered value has to keep the datatype its tag names, or it is not a value this
-- pass understands. The string "false" for `Visible` is truthy everywhere downstream
-- (flatten_node hides a node only on a real boolean false), so recovering `Visible` as
-- text turned a hidden object into a visible one, in silence. Scalars convert; anything
-- else (Ref, token, structs like UDim2/Color3) keeps the file's text as before, and a
-- struct the bridge cannot read is named in `unreadable` rather than guessed at.
local function from_xml(tag, text)
  if tag == "bool" then return text == "true" end
  if tag == "int" or tag == "int64" or tag == "float" or tag == "double" then
    return tonumber(text)
  end
  return unescape(text)
end

local function xml_props(inst, shallow)
  local target = inst
  local clone = nil
  if shallow then
    local okClone, cloned = pcall(function() return inst:Clone() end)
    if not okClone or cloned == nil then return {}, {} end
    clone = cloned
    target = clone
    for _, child in ipairs(clone:GetChildren()) do child:Destroy() end
  end
  local ok, xml = pcall(function() return roblox.serializeModel({ target }, { xml = true }) end)
  if clone ~= nil then clone:Destroy() end
  if not ok then return {}, {} end
  -- first <Properties> block belongs to this instance, children come after it
  local block = string.match(xml, "<Properties>(.-)</Properties>")
  local found, present = {}, {}
  if block then
    for tag, name, value in string.gmatch(block, "<([%w]+) name=\"([%w_]+)\">([^<]*)</") do
      present[name] = true
      if value ~= "" and found[name] == nil then found[name] = from_xml(tag, value) end
    end
    -- Content values nest the URI: <Content name="Image"><uri>rbxassetid://123</uri>
    for name, value in string.gmatch(block, "name=\"([%w_]+)\"><[uU][rR][lL]>(.-)</[uU][rR][lL]>") do
      present[name] = true
      if value ~= "" and found[name] == nil then found[name] = unescape(value) end
    end
    for name in string.gmatch(block, "<[%w]+ name=\"([%w_]+)\"") do
      present[name] = true
    end
  end
  return found, present
end

local function parse_property_block(block)
  local found, present = {}, {}
  for tag, name, value in string.gmatch(block, "<([%w]+) name=\"([%w_]+)\">([^<]*)</") do
    present[name] = true
    if value ~= "" and found[name] == nil then found[name] = from_xml(tag, value) end
  end
  for name, value in string.gmatch(block, "name=\"([%w_]+)\"><[uU][rR][lL]>(.-)</[uU][rR][lL]>") do
    present[name] = true
    if value ~= "" and found[name] == nil then found[name] = unescape(value) end
  end
  for name in string.gmatch(block, "<[%w]+ name=\"([%w_]+)\"") do
    present[name] = true
  end
  return found, present
end

-- `xml_props` below serializes one instance *and its whole subtree* per call, and it
-- is called once per instance: that is O(nodes x subtree) native work, and stubbing
-- it out took AnimationEditorGUI's emit from 6217ms to 5018ms. The file's text is in
-- memory, rbx-dom writes items in tree order, so one serialization of the whole
-- model answers every instance. Item N is instance N only if rbx-dom keeps that
-- order, so the class attribute of every item is checked against the tree before
-- the index is used; any doubt and the per-instance call stays in charge.
local function xml_visual_index(roots, classes, keep_map, wanted)
  -- Fast profiles only need XML fallback values for retained visual nodes. Clone the
  -- retained roots once, prune runtime-only subtrees from the clones, and serialize
  -- that reduced tree. Originals are never mutated.
  local clones = {}
  local prune_ok = true
  local function prune(original, clone)
    local original_children = original:GetChildren()
    local clone_children = clone:GetChildren()
    if #original_children ~= #clone_children then
      prune_ok = false
      return
    end
    for idx = 1, #original_children do
      local original_child = original_children[idx]
      local clone_child = clone_children[idx]
      if keep_map[original_child] then
        prune(original_child, clone_child)
      else
        clone_child:Destroy()
      end
    end
  end
  for _, root in ipairs(roots) do
    if keep_map[root] then
      local ok_clone, clone = pcall(function() return root:Clone() end)
      if not ok_clone or clone == nil then
        prune_ok = false
        break
      end
      prune(root, clone)
      table.insert(clones, clone)
    end
  end
  if not prune_ok then
    for _, clone in ipairs(clones) do clone:Destroy() end
    return nil
  end
  local ok, xml = pcall(function() return roblox.serializeModel(clones, { xml = true }) end)
  for _, clone in ipairs(clones) do clone:Destroy() end
  if not ok then return nil end
  local items, count, pos = {}, 0, 1
  while true do
    local s, e, close, tag = string.find(xml, "<(/?)([A-Za-z]+)", pos)
    if not s then break end
    if tag == "Item" and close == "" then
      count = count + 1
      local cls = string.match(string.sub(xml, e + 1, e + 64), "class=\"([%w_]+)\"")
      items[count] = { class = cls, found = {}, present = {} }
      pos = e + 1
    elseif tag == "Properties" and close == "" then
      local stop = string.find(xml, "</Properties>", e + 1, true)
      local cur = items[count]
      if cur and (wanted == nil or wanted[count]) then
        local block = string.sub(xml, e + 1, (stop or #xml + 1) - 1)
        for name in pairs(VISUAL_XML_RECOVERY) do
          if string.find(block, 'name="' .. name .. '"', 1, true) then
            cur.present[name] = true
            local tagName, value =
              string.match(block, '<([%w]+) name="' .. name .. '">([^<]*)</')
            if tagName ~= nil and value ~= nil and value ~= "" then
              cur.found[name] = from_xml(tagName, value)
            end
          end
        end
      end
      pos = stop and stop + 13 or (e + 1)
    else
      pos = e + 1
    end
  end
  if count ~= #classes then
    print("visual xml index: rejected, " .. tostring(count) .. " items for "
      .. tostring(#classes) .. " instances; using shallow fallback")
    return nil
  end
  for idx = 1, count do
    if items[idx].class ~= classes[idx] then
      print("visual xml index: rejected at item " .. tostring(idx) .. "; using shallow fallback")
      return nil
    end
  end
  return items
end

local function xml_index(roots, classes, wanted)
  local ok, xml = pcall(function() return roblox.serializeModel(roots, { xml = true }) end)
  if not ok then return nil end
  local items, count, pos = {}, 0, 1
  while true do
    local s, e, close, tag = string.find(xml, "<(/?)([A-Za-z]+)", pos)
    if not s then break end
    if tag == "Item" and close == "" then
      count = count + 1
      local cls = string.match(string.sub(xml, e + 1, e + 64), "class=\"([%w_]+)\"")
      items[count] = { class = cls, found = {}, present = {} }
      pos = e + 1
    elseif tag == "Properties" and close == "" then
      local stop = string.find(xml, "</Properties>", e + 1, true)
      local cur = items[count]
      if cur and (wanted == nil or wanted[count]) then
        cur.found, cur.present =
          parse_property_block(string.sub(xml, e + 1, (stop or #xml + 1) - 1))
      end
      pos = stop and stop + 13 or (e + 1)
    else
      pos = e + 1
    end
  end
  if count ~= #classes then
    print("xml index: rejected, " .. tostring(count) .. " items for " .. tostring(#classes)
      .. " instances; falling back to one serialization per instance")
    return nil
  end
  for idx = 1, count do
    if items[idx].class ~= classes[idx] then
      print("xml index: rejected, item " .. tostring(idx) .. " is a " .. tostring(items[idx].class)
        .. " where the tree has a " .. tostring(classes[idx]) .. "; falling back")
      return nil
    end
  end
  return items
end

local function preorder_classes(roots, keep_map)
  local out = {}
  local function rec(inst)
    if keep_map ~= nil and not keep_map[inst] then return end
    table.insert(out, inst.ClassName)
    for _, child in ipairs(inst:GetChildren()) do rec(child) end
  end
  for _, r in ipairs(roots) do rec(r) end
  return out
end

-- Arguments: this chunk's own (rhr-ir-serve.luau runs it once per file in one Lune
-- process), else the command line's.
local ARGS = table.pack(...)
local serving = ARGS.n > 0
if not serving then ARGS = process.args end
-- A failure ends a command-line run with exit code 1; a served one reports it.
local function fail()
  if serving then error("rhr-ir failed", 0) end
  process.exit(1)
end
local emission_profile = ARGS[3] or "full"
local node_index = 0
local visual_keep = {}

-- XML recovery, deferred. A property the bridge will not hand over is looked up in
-- the XML view of the same instance. Serializing the whole place up front cost a
-- 116k-part place 46 s and most of its 6 GB peak, for one value (Lighting.ClockTime)
-- in the 3D profile. So the walk only notes which (instance, names) need it, and the
-- XML is made afterwards, for those alone.
--
-- In a binary file every instance of a class carries the same saved properties (the
-- format stores them per class), so one shallow serialization per class says which
-- names the XML can ever answer; the others are never looked up. An XML source file
-- can differ per instance, so there every miss is looked up, as before.
local binary_source = false
local class_xml_present = {}
local pending_recovery = {}
-- Up to this many instances are serialized one by one; more, and one serialization
-- of the whole (retained) tree answers them all.
local PER_INSTANCE_LIMIT = 2000

-- Per class: the allowlisted names worth visiting (a property of the class, or a
-- name its saved XML carries) and the names its XML carries. Visiting only these
-- instead of all of PROPS matters on big places: 370 names x 180k instances.
local function class_plan(inst, valid)
  local plan = class_xml_present[inst.ClassName]
  if plan ~= nil then return plan end
  if not binary_source then
    plan = { names = PROPS, present = nil }
  else
    local _, present = xml_props(inst, true)
    local names = {}
    for _, name in ipairs(PROPS) do
      if valid[name] or present[name] then table.insert(names, name) end
    end
    plan = { names = names, present = present }
  end
  class_xml_present[inst.ClassName] = plan
  return plan
end

local function read_property(inst, name)
  return inst[name]
end

-- Identity. Every instance gets a numeric id (preorder over the whole file, so it
-- does not depend on the profile) and a unique slash path. Siblings that share a
-- name are ALL indexed, `Card[1]`, `Card[2]`, so a bare name is never ambiguous and
-- no consumer can silently pick (or overwrite) the wrong one. References carry the
-- target's id in `node.refs`, next to the readable GetFullName() string in props.
local instance_ids, instance_paths = {}, {}
local next_id = 0
local function assign_identity(instances, parent_path)
  local counts, seen = {}, {}
  local function segment_name(inst)
    return inst.Name ~= "" and inst.Name or inst.ClassName
  end
  for _, inst in ipairs(instances) do
    local name = segment_name(inst)
    counts[name] = (counts[name] or 0) + 1
  end
  for _, inst in ipairs(instances) do
    local name = segment_name(inst)
    local segment = name
    if counts[name] > 1 then
      seen[name] = (seen[name] or 0) + 1
      segment = name .. "[" .. tostring(seen[name]) .. "]"
    end
    next_id = next_id + 1
    instance_ids[inst] = next_id
    local here = parent_path == "" and segment or (parent_path .. "/" .. segment)
    instance_paths[inst] = here
    assign_identity(inst:GetChildren(), here)
  end
end

local function new_node(inst, props, refs)
  local node = {
    id = instance_ids[inst],
    path = instance_paths[inst],
    className = inst.ClassName,
    name = inst.Name,
    props = props,
    children = {},
  }
  if refs and next(refs) then node.refs = refs end
  return node
end

local function walk(inst)
  if emission_profile ~= "full" and not visual_keep[inst] then return nil end
  node_index = node_index + 1
  local children = inst:GetChildren()

  -- A non-visual ancestor is retained only to preserve hierarchy/full-name paths.
  if emission_profile ~= "full" and not profile_keeps_class(emission_profile, inst.ClassName) then
    local node = new_node(inst, {}, nil)
    for _, child in ipairs(children) do
      local child_node = walk(child)
      if child_node ~= nil then table.insert(node.children, child_node) end
    end
    return node
  end

  local valid = class_property_set(inst.ClassName)
  verify_class(inst, valid)
  local plan = class_plan(inst, valid)
  -- Allowlisted names that this class has no property for but a child is called:
  -- the bridge answers `frame.Padding` with the *child* of that name, and feeding
  -- that on is worse than dropping it (flatten_node is name-driven, so a Frame with
  -- a child named "Text" would render the word "Instance"). Named, not read.
  local child_named = {}
  for _, child in ipairs(children) do
    if PROPS_SET[child.Name] and not valid[child.Name] then
      child_named[child.Name] = child.ClassName
    end
  end
  local props = {}
  local refs = {}
  local recover = {}
  local unmapped = {}
  local not_a_property = {}
  -- A child named like a property of another class is reported (not_a_property)
  -- in allowlist order, so such an instance visits every name.
  local visit = next(child_named) and PROPS or plan.names
  local xml_present = plan.present
  for _, name in ipairs(visit) do
    local ok, value, child_fallback
    if valid[name] then
      ok, value = pcall(read_property, inst, name)
    else
      -- Not a property of this class: no read, no error, no stack traceback. It
      -- can still be a child's name, which the map above already knows about.
      child_fallback = child_named[name]
    end
    if value ~= nil and typeof(value) == "Instance" then
      if name == "Adornee" or name == "Attachment0" or name == "Attachment1" or name == "PrimaryPart" then
        -- Preserve references as stable names; the browser resolves them in-tree.
        refs[name] = instance_ids[value]
        local okName, fullName = pcall(function() return value:GetFullName() end)
        if okName and fullName ~= nil then value = fullName else value = nil end
      else
        -- An instance here is usually a child whose name collided with a
        -- reflected property. Do not feed it to the flatten schema.
        child_fallback = value.ClassName
        value = nil
      end
    end
    if valid[name] and (not ok or value == nil) then
      -- Roblox renamed the ContentId properties (`Image` -> `ImageContent`). In
      -- current rbx-dom builds the legacy name has no default value and cannot be
      -- read at all, while the renamed one reads fine. Report it under the legacy
      -- name so the flatten schema, which keys off `Image`, still applies.
      local content_name = CONTENT_PROPERTY_ALIASES[name] or (name .. "Content")
      local ok2, value2 = pcall(function() return inst[content_name] end)
      if ok2 and value2 ~= nil and typeof(value2) ~= "Instance" then
        ok, value, child_fallback = true, value2, nil
      end
    end
    if ok and value ~= nil then
      local c = conv(value)
      if c ~= nil then
        props[name] = c
      elseif typeof(value) ~= "Content" then
        -- Unmappable datatype. Name it on the node instead of dropping it: an
        -- empty Content is the one value that legitimately disappears.
        table.insert(unmapped, name .. " (" .. typeof(value) .. ")")
      end
    elseif child_fallback then
      -- Not a property of this class at all: the name belongs to a child. Nothing
      -- was lost, so this is informational, not a drop.
      table.insert(not_a_property, name .. " (child " .. child_fallback .. ")")
    elseif (emission_profile == "full" or VISUAL_XML_RECOVERY[name]) and (xml_present == nil or xml_present[name]) then
      -- Looked up in the XML after the walk (see pending_recovery).
      table.insert(recover, name)
    end
  end
  if inst.ClassName == "UnionOperation" and (props.AssetId == nil or props.AssetId == "") then
    -- A union not uploaded yet keeps its render mesh in the file itself (binary, so
    -- base64 for JSON); rhr.unions decodes it.
    local okMesh, mesh = pcall(function() return inst.MeshData2 end)
    if okMesh and type(mesh) == "string" and #mesh > 0 and #mesh < 16 * 1024 * 1024 then
      props.MeshData2 = base64(mesh)
    end
  end
  local node = new_node(inst, props, refs)
  if ATTRIBUTE_CLASSES[inst.ClassName] then
    local okAttrs, attrs = pcall(function() return inst:GetAttributes() end)
    if okAttrs and attrs and next(attrs) then
      local kept = {}
      for key, value in attrs do
        -- Numbers and switches only: that is all the convention uses, and a string
        -- attribute can hold raw bytes that JSON cannot carry.
        local kind = typeof(value)
        if kind == "number" then kept[key] = finite(value) elseif kind == "boolean" then kept[key] = value end
      end
      if next(kept) then node.attributes = kept end
    end
  end
  -- `RhrIgnore`: which `rhr check` findings to leave out here (rhr.checks).
  local okIgnore, ignore = pcall(function() return inst:GetAttribute("RhrIgnore") end)
  if okIgnore and type(ignore) == "string" and ignore ~= "" then node.rhrIgnore = ignore end
  if #recover > 0 then
    table.insert(pending_recovery, { inst = inst, index = node_index, node = node, names = recover })
  end
  if #unmapped > 0 then node.unmapped = unmapped end
  if #not_a_property > 0 then node.not_a_property = not_a_property end
  for _, child in ipairs(children) do
    local child_node = walk(child)
    if child_node ~= nil then table.insert(node.children, child_node) end
  end
  return node
end

local path, out = ARGS[1], ARGS[2]
if not path or not out or (emission_profile ~= "full" and emission_profile ~= "visual" and emission_profile ~= "static") then
  print("usage: lune run src/rhr/luau/rhr-ir.luau <source.rbxm|.rbxmx|.rbxl> <out.json> [full|visual|static]")
  fail()
end
local data = fs.readFile(path)
-- An XML declaration (`<?xml version="1.0"?>`, which some tools write before <roblox>)
-- makes rbx-dom's format detection give up; Studio reads such files, so drop it.
if string.sub(data, 1, 5) == "<?xml" then
  local close = string.find(data, "?>", 1, true)
  if close then data = string.gsub(string.sub(data, close + 2), "^%s+", "") end
end
local roots
local ok = pcall(function() roots = roblox.deserializeModel(data) end)
if not ok then roots = roblox.deserializePlace(data) end
local node_classes = preorder_classes(roots)
assign_identity(roots, "")
if emission_profile ~= "full" then
  local function mark(inst)
    local keep = profile_keeps_class(emission_profile, inst.ClassName)
    for _, child in ipairs(inst:GetChildren()) do
      keep = mark(child) or keep
    end
    visual_keep[inst] = keep
    return keep
  end
  for _, root in ipairs(roots) do mark(root) end
end
binary_source = string.sub(data, 1, 8) == "<roblox!"
local nodes = {}
for _, r in ipairs(roots) do
  local node = walk(r)
  if node ~= nil then table.insert(nodes, node) end
end

-- Recover what the bridge would not hand over, from the XML view of each instance.
if #pending_recovery > 0 then
  local xml_items = nil
  if #pending_recovery > PER_INSTANCE_LIMIT then
    local wanted = {}
    for _, entry in ipairs(pending_recovery) do wanted[entry.index] = true end
    if emission_profile == "full" then
      xml_items = xml_index(roots, node_classes, wanted)
    else
      xml_items = xml_visual_index(roots, preorder_classes(roots, visual_keep), visual_keep, wanted)
    end
  end
  for _, entry in ipairs(pending_recovery) do
    local found, present
    local item = xml_items and xml_items[entry.index]
    if item ~= nil then
      if item.class ~= entry.inst.ClassName then
        error("emitter: the XML index does not line up at instance " .. tostring(entry.index))
      end
      found, present = item.found, item.present
    else
      found, present = xml_props(entry.inst, true)
    end
    local unreadable = {}
    for _, name in ipairs(entry.names) do
      local raw = found[name]
      if raw ~= nil then
        entry.node.props[name] = raw
      elseif emission_profile == "full" and present[name] then
        -- the file carries it, the bridge will not hand it over, nothing to
        -- recover it from: name it rather than dropping it in silence
        table.insert(unreadable, name)
      end
    end
    if #unreadable > 0 then entry.node.unreadable = unreadable end
  end
end

-- The JSON is written node by node: encoding the whole tree in one call made a second
-- full copy of it, which took a 116k-part place from 2.7 to over 5 GB. Each node is
-- encoded without its children, which follow inside it; a subtree is let go once it
-- is written. Same encoder, same document.
local function write_ir()
  local parts = {}
  local function emit(node)
    local children = node.children
    node.children = nil
    local head = serde.encode("json", node)
    table.insert(parts, string.sub(head, 1, -2))
    if #children == 0 then
      -- An empty Lua table encodes as an object; keep the document as it was.
      table.insert(parts, ',"children":{}}')
      return
    end
    table.insert(parts, ',"children":[')
    for index, child in ipairs(children) do
      if index > 1 then table.insert(parts, ",") end
      emit(child)
      children[index] = false
    end
    table.insert(parts, "]}")
  end
  local header = serde.encode("json", { schema = "rhr.ir/1", sourcePath = path })
  table.insert(parts, string.sub(header, 1, -2))
  if #nodes == 0 then
    fs.writeFile(out, table.concat(parts) .. ',"roots":{}}')
    return
  end
  table.insert(parts, ',"roots":[')
  for index, root in ipairs(nodes) do
    if index > 1 then table.insert(parts, ",") end
    emit(root)
    nodes[index] = false
  end
  table.insert(parts, "]}")
  fs.writeFile(out, table.concat(parts))
end

-- Never silent: report properties the file carries that we could not read, and
-- properties whose datatype we could not map. Either one is a rendering bug
-- waiting to happen, so the counts print on every run.
local names, unmapped_names = {}, {}
local nodes_affected, unmapped_nodes, collision_nodes = 0, 0, 0
local function count(node)
  if node.unreadable then
    nodes_affected = nodes_affected + 1
    for _, name in ipairs(node.unreadable) do names[name] = (names[name] or 0) + 1 end
  end
  if node.unmapped then
    unmapped_nodes = unmapped_nodes + 1
    for _, name in ipairs(node.unmapped) do unmapped_names[name] = (unmapped_names[name] or 0) + 1 end
  end
  if node.not_a_property then
    collision_nodes = collision_nodes + 1
  end
  for _, child in ipairs(node.children) do count(child) end
end
for _, r in ipairs(nodes) do count(r) end
local root_count = #nodes
write_ir()
local function tally(counts)
  local out = {}
  for name, n in pairs(counts) do table.insert(out, name .. "x" .. tostring(n)) end
  table.sort(out)
  return table.concat(out, ", ")
end
print("wrote " .. out .. " roots=" .. root_count)
print("unreadable: " .. tostring(nodes_affected) .. " nodes"
  .. (next(names) and (", " .. tally(names)) or ""))
print("unmapped: " .. tostring(unmapped_nodes) .. " nodes"
  .. (next(unmapped_names) and (", " .. tally(unmapped_names)) or ""))
-- Property names that are really child names (a Frame with a child called
-- "Padding" answers frame.Padding with the child). Nothing was dropped; the count
-- is here so a sudden jump is visible.
print("name collisions: " .. tostring(collision_nodes) .. " nodes")
-- The class filter is one table lookup away from losing a property, so its answer is
-- checked against a full read of the first instance of every class (see verify_class).
local unknown_count = 0
for _ in pairs(unknown_classes) do unknown_count = unknown_count + 1 end
print("class filter: " .. tostring(#node_classes) .. " instances over "
  .. tostring(filter_mismatches.narrow + filter_mismatches.wide) .. " database mismatches"
  .. (#filter_mismatches.names > 0 and (", e.g. " .. table.concat(filter_mismatches.names, ", ")) or "")
  .. (unknown_count > 0 and (", " .. tostring(unknown_count) .. " class(es) not in the database read in full") or ""))
-- A "narrow" mismatch is a value the bridge hands over for a name the database does
-- not list for that class: the filter would skip it on every other instance, so the
-- IR above is missing properties. Refuse it rather than ship it.
if filter_mismatches.narrow > 0 then
  print("emitter: the reflection database is narrower than the bridge on "
    .. tostring(filter_mismatches.narrow) .. " names; the IR written to " .. out
    .. " may be missing them")
  fail()
end

--
--   lune run story-runtime.luau <built.rbxl|rbxm> <module path JSON> <out.rbxm> <width> <height> <name>
--
-- The built file is the Rojo project; the module path (a JSON list of names from the
-- root) is the story's ModuleScript in it. Every UI library ends in the same calls
-- (Instance.new, set properties, parent), so this copies the Roblox side, not any
-- library: Lune's own instances (properties, datatypes, Enums, saving), plus events,
-- the services UI code touches, instance-based require, and a frame loop that lets
-- the UI settle. Story forms: function(target) (Hoarcekat, UI Labs); UI Labs tables
-- with react/reactRoblox, roact, fusion, vide or a generic render; Flipbook's table.
-- Scripts' own threads are left behind: the process exits once the UI is saved.

-- Signals ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Library code checks typeof(x) == "RBXScriptSignal": the sandbox's typeof reads __type.
local Signal = { __type = "RBXScriptSignal" }
Signal.__index = Signal
local Connection = { __type = "RBXScriptConnection" }
Connection.__index = Connection

function Signal.new()
	return setmetatable({ handlers = {} }, Signal)
end
function Signal:Connect(fn)
	local connection = setmetatable({ Connected = true }, Connection)
	local handlers = self.handlers
	handlers[connection] = fn
	function connection.Disconnect()
		connection.Connected = false
		handlers[connection] = nil
	end
	connection.disconnect = connection.Disconnect
	return connection
end
Signal.connect = Signal.Connect
function Signal:Once(fn)
	local connection
	connection = self:Connect(function(...)
		connection.Disconnect()
		fn(...)
	end)
	return connection
end
function Signal:Fire(...)
	for _, fn in self.handlers do
		task.spawn(fn, ...)
	end
end
function Signal:Wait()
	local thread = coroutine.running()
	self:Once(function(...)
		task.spawn(thread, ...)
	end)
	return coroutine.yield()
end

local signals = setmetatable({}, { __mode = "k" })
local function eventOf(instance, key)
	local byKey = signals[instance]
	if not byKey then
		byKey = {}
		signals[instance] = byKey
	end
	local signal = byKey[key]
	if not signal then
		signal = Signal.new()
		byKey[key] = signal
	end
	return signal
end

local loaded, loading = {}, {}

local function requireModule(target, from)
	if typeof(target) ~= "Instance" then
		error(`require({typeof(target)}) is not supported when running a story (only ModuleScripts in the project)`, 3)
	end
	if not target:IsA("ModuleScript") then
		error(`{target:GetFullName()} is not a ModuleScript`, 3)
	end
	if loaded[target] ~= nil then
		return loaded[target]
	end
	if loading[target] then
		error(`require loop at {target:GetFullName()}`, 3)
	end
	loading[target] = true
	local environment = table.clone(base) -- (copied: Lune's load() sets its own metatable)
	environment.script = target
	environment.require = function(module)
		return requireModule(module, target)
	end
	local chunk = luau.load(target.Source, { debugName = target:GetFullName(), environment = environment })
	local result = chunk()
	loading[target] = nil
	loaded[target] = if result == nil then true else result
	return result
end

local function controlDefaults(controls)
	local values = {}
	for name, control in controls or {} do
		if type(control) == "table" then
			local value = control.ControlValue
			if value == nil then value = control.Default end
			if value == nil then value = control.default end
			if value == nil then value = control.__default end
			if value == nil and type(control.List) == "table" then value = control.List[1] end
			values[name] = value
		else
			values[name] = control
		end
	end
	return values
end

local function mount()
	local story = requireModule(storyScript)
	if type(story) == "function" then
		return story(target)
	end
	if type(story) ~= "table" then
		error("a story module returns a function(target) or a story table; this one returned a " .. typeof(story))
	end
	local controls = controlDefaults(story.controls)
	local props = { target = target, controls = controls, converted = {}, subscribe = function()
		return function() end
	end }
	if story.react and story.reactRoblox then
		local React, ReactRoblox = story.react, story.reactRoblox
		local element = story.story
		if type(element) == "function" then
			element = React.createElement(element, props)
		end
		local root = if story.renderer == "legacy" and ReactRoblox.createLegacyRoot
			then ReactRoblox.createLegacyRoot(target)
			else ReactRoblox.createRoot(target)
		root:render(element)
		return
	end
	if story.roact then
		local Roact = story.roact
		local element = story.story
		if type(element) == "function" then
			element = Roact.createElement(element, props)
		end
		Roact.mount(element, target)
		return
	end
	if story.vide then
		story.vide.mount(function()
			return story.story(props)
		end, target)
		return
	end
	if type(story.render) == "function" then
		return story.render(props)
	end
	if story.fusion and type(story.story) == "function" then
		props.scope = story.fusion.scoped and story.fusion.scoped(story.fusion)
		return story.story(props)
	end
	if type(story.story) == "function" then
		return story.story(target, props)
	end
	error("a story table needs react + reactRoblox, roact, vide, fusion, a render function or a story function")
end
